title: Chapter 9 Problem Set: Fault-Tolerant ETS Session Store with Heir Failover
solutionExplanation: Implements a fault-tolerant session cache architecture using a supervisor, an heir table manager, and a gen_server worker with atomic hit tracking.

otpDocCards.description: Transfers ownership of an ETS table to another process without table destruction.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why should table_manager be started BEFORE session_cache in the supervision child specification list?

options.label: Supervisors fail compilation if workers are not alphabetical.
options.explanation: Supervisor child specifications can be listed in any arbitrary order.

options.label: session_cache needs whereis(table_manager) to return a live PID when it specifies the {heir, HeirPid, Data} option in ets:new/2.
options.explanation: Because session_cache configures {heir, whereis(table_manager), Tag} upon creating the ETS table, table_manager must already be registered and running.

options.label: table_manager creates the ETS table and inserts mock data.
options.explanation: session_cache creates the active ETS table and uses table_manager solely as heir guardian.

options.label: table_manager is a supervisor, so it must start before workers.
options.explanation: table_manager is a worker gen_server, not a supervisor.
